summary: Defines a textual representation for Autonomous System numbers as the plain decimal value, to be used by all documents, systems and user interfaces. This is a Proposed Standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines a consistent way to write Autonomous System numbers: use the number's decimal value as one uninterrupted string. It distinguishes this asplain form from two dotted forms.

asplain format for autonomous system numbers
how should an autonomous system number be written

subtitle: A single decimal notation for writing Autonomous System numbers.

tldr.problem: Multiple textual forms for Autonomous System numbers can cause confusion in documentation, configuration, and tools.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC proposes asplain: write the AS number as one decimal integer without a delimiter.
tldr.outcome: The RFC says IANA registries should use decimal representation for AS numbers.

today: RFC 5396 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Choose One Textual Form
sections.content:
The RFC proposes decimal notation for Autonomous System numbers in documents, systems, and user interfaces. It calls this form asplain.

The document notes other formats in use: asdot+ splits the number into two decimal values joined by a period, while asdot uses plain notation below 65536 and asdot+ for larger values.
sections.plainLanguage: One number can be written in several ways. The RFC proposes one consistent form to avoid confusion.

sections.title: Three Representation Formats
sections.content:
asplain writes every AS number as a decimal integer, such as 65546. asdot+ writes two decimal components separated by a period, such as 1.10. asdot uses asplain below 65536 and asdot+ for values equal to or above 65536.

The RFC proposes asplain because it presents the AS number as a single value without field delimiters.
sections.plainLanguage: Asplain is one continuous decimal number. The other notations add a period and divide the number into parts.

sections.title: The Proposed Standard Representation
sections.content:
The document proposes asplain for documentation, configuration systems, reports, external tools, and information repositories. It says IANA registries should use decimal representation.

The security section says the document does not address security matters associated with routing systems.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC recommends writing AS numbers as decimal values in registries and other text. It does not define a routing security mechanism.
